subject: art-design
title: Sculpture & 3D: Foundations
welcome_lead: Meet sculpture's four big processes — modelling, carving, casting and constructing.
meta_desc: GCSE sculpture foundations: modelling, carving, casting, constructing and key artists.
final_note: Knowing the process names lets you read any 3D work.

concepts.def: Building up soft material like clay.
Cutting away from a solid block.
Hard copper-tin alloy ideal for casting.
Aged surface colour on metal sculpture.

walkthroughs.body_html: Modelling adds material — clay, plasticine, wax. Carving takes it away — stone, wood, soap. Rodin modelled The Thinker in clay (cast in bronze, 1902). Michelangelo carved David from a single marble block (1501-04).

Casting turns a soft positive into a hard copy. Lost-wax casting melts a wax model out of a mould, then pours molten bronze in. Once cooled and cleaned, the bronze develops a coloured patina over years.

Modern sculptors often construct — bolting, welding or weaving rigid parts together. Picasso's bull's head joined a bicycle saddle and handlebars. Construction allowed assemblage and the rise of mixed-media 3D in the 20th century.
